note.en: What you see: Withdrawn slightly above the mid oesophageal station, the sector cuts the aortic valve in cross section so all three cusps appear as a triangle opening in systole. The left atrium wraps behind, with the right atrium and right ventricular outflow to the side and the interatrial septum between them. Leaflet tips meet in the centre in diastole. This is the plane for counting cusps and judging symmetry of opening before any long axis measurement.

steps.en: What you see: Withdrawn slightly above the mid oesophageal station, the sector cuts the aortic valve in cross section so all three cusps appear as a triangle opening in systole. The left atrium wraps behind, with the right atrium and right ventricular outflow to the side and the interatrial septum between them. Leaflet tips meet in the centre in diastole. This is the plane for counting cusps and judging symmetry of opening before any long axis measurement.
Landmarks to confirm: Left, right and non coronary cusps of the aortic valve, left atrium cavity, right atrium cavity, right ventricle cavity, interatrial septum, oesophagus behind the left atrium.

Common mistakes and correction: Oblique cut that makes three cusps look like two: adjust withdrawal and rotation until all three cusps match in size. Probe too high so the valve drops out toward the arch: advance slightly. Right coronary cusp dropout mimicking an abscess cavity: confirm with the long axis plane before reporting pathology.

Normal values with units: Probe depth about 25 to 30 cm from the incisors. Multiplane angle near 45 degrees. In health all three cusps open symmetrically in systole and meet centrally in diastole. A valve area below 1.0 cm2, or a peak jet velocity of 4.0 m per s or above with a mean gradient of 40 mmHg or above, marks severe stenosis.

Pitfalls: Rheumatic heart disease is common in India, so commissural fusion with a triangular systolic orifice in a young patient points toward rheumatic aortic involvement and needs full quantification. Bicuspid valves can look tricuspid in one frame, so confirm cusp number across the cycle. Heavy calcification throws shadows that hide cusps, so lower gain and sweep before judging severity.

todo.en: How to get it step by step: From the mid oesophageal four chamber, withdraw the probe slightly toward 25 to 30 cm from the incisors and rotate the multiplane to about 45 degrees. Centre the valve and fine tune a few degrees until all three cusps show equal size in systole. Freeze in systole to judge opening symmetry and in diastole to judge closure. If only two cusps show, the cut sits oblique, so adjust withdrawal and rotation together until the third cusp opens.

q.en: How is the aortic valve short axis obtained from the four chamber station?

o.en: Withdraw slightly and rotate to about 45 degrees
Rotate to 120 degrees without moving the probe

why.en: Slight withdrawal with multiplane near 45 degrees brings the valve into short axis.

q.en: What confirms a true symmetric short axis cut?

o.en: Three cusps of equal size in systole

why.en: A true cut shows three cusps of equal size opening symmetrically in systole.

q.en: Which finding marks severe aortic stenosis?

o.en: Peak velocity below 1.0 m per s

why.en: A valve area below 1.0 cm2 marks severe stenosis.

q.en: A young patient shows commissural fusion with a triangular orifice. What next?

o.en: Report a bicuspid valve at once
Confirm cusp number across the cycle with full quantification

why.en: Rheumatic involvement is common in India and cusp number must be confirmed across the cycle with quantification.
